ingredients.name: Semaglutide
ingredients.whatItDoes: A GLP-1 receptor agonist that mimics the body's natural satiety hormone, reducing appetite and slowing gastric emptying.
ingredients.whyItMatters: Semaglutide works at the level of the brain's appetite centers, reducing hunger in a way that willpower alone cannot replicate. Clinical trials show 10-15% average body weight reduction over 12-16 weeks.

personas.headline: You've tried everything and the weight isn't moving
personas.detail: GLP-1 medications work differently from diets or exercise — they change your brain's relationship with food. Many people describe the absence of food noise as transformative.

personas.headline: Your doctor has recommended addressing your weight for health reasons
personas.detail: Obesity is associated with dozens of downstream health risks. Semaglutide has more clinical evidence for sustainable weight loss than any other prescription option currently available.

whatToExpect.onset: Reduced appetite typically noticed within the first week. Meaningful weight loss usually begins in weeks 2-4.
whatToExpect.duration: Weekly subcutaneous injections, administered in-office or self-administered at home.
whatToExpect.frequency: Once weekly. This is an ongoing program, not a one-time treatment.
whatToExpect.howItFeels: A small injection, typically in the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm. Most people find it comfortable. Nausea is the most common early side effect and usually resolves within 2-4 weeks.

glp1.mechanism: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) receptor agonist. Mimics the body's natural post-meal satiety signal, suppressing appetite and slowing digestion.

eligibility.bmiRequirement: BMI 27+ with a weight-related condition (hypertension, diabetes, high cholesterol), or BMI 30+ without comorbidities
contraindications: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma

serious: Pancreatitis — seek immediate care for severe abdominal pain
Rare: thyroid tumors (based on animal data)
sideEffects.managementTips: Nausea is dramatically reduced by eating smaller meals, avoiding fatty or spicy foods, and staying hydrated. Most patients adapt within 3-4 weeks.

glp1.monitoring: Initial consult + monthly check-ins to assess weight loss, side effects, and dose adjustments.

ingredients.whyItMatters: Clinical trials show tirzepatide produces 20-22% average body weight reduction — the highest of any approved weight loss medication. The dual mechanism provides broader metabolic benefits including improved insulin sensitivity.

personas.headline: You want the most effective medical weight loss option currently available

personas.headline: You have type 2 diabetes or metabolic syndrome alongside your weight goals
personas.detail: The GIP component of tirzepatide provides additional metabolic benefits including improved insulin sensitivity and glucose control — making it particularly valuable for those with metabolic conditions.

whatToExpect.onset: Appetite reduction usually noticed within the first week. Weight loss typically becomes apparent by weeks 3-4.

glp1.mechanism: Dual GLP-1 and GIP (glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide) receptor agonist. Activates two complementary gut hormone pathways for enhanced appetite suppression and improved insulin sensitivity.

eligibility.bmiRequirement: BMI 27+ with a weight-related condition, or BMI 30+ without comorbidities

serious: Pancreatitis — seek immediate care for severe abdominal pain
Rare: thyroid tumors (based on animal data)

glp1.monitoring: Initial consult + monthly check-ins for weight tracking, side effect management, and dose optimization.

ingredients.name: Methylcobalamin B12
ingredients.whatItDoes: The active, bioavailable form of B12 that your cells can use immediately — supports red blood cell formation, neurological function, and DNA synthesis. Delivered intramuscularly, absorption is complete and does not depend on stomach acid, intrinsic factor, or small intestine uptake.
ingredients.whyItMatters: Methylcobalamin is significantly better absorbed than cyanocobalamin. IM injection bypasses the stomach, intrinsic factor, and ileal transport entirely -- achieving near-complete absorption regardless of gut health. This is critical for gastric bypass and sleeve patients, those on PPIs or metformin, and people with IBD, Crohn's, or celiac disease.

personas.headline: You feel tired more than you should
personas.detail: B12 deficiency is one of the most common and most overlooked causes of persistent fatigue. It's especially common in vegetarians, vegans, people over 50 with reduced stomach acid, gastric bypass or sleeve patients, and anyone on long-term PPIs or metformin -- because all of these conditions impair oral B12 absorption.

personas.headline: You want a quick energy boost without a full IV
personas.detail: The B12 shot is our fastest, most affordable treatment — a 2-minute injection that many people report feeling within a few hours.

whatToExpect.onset: Some people notice increased energy within a few hours. The full effect builds over 24-48 hours as B12 enters the cells.
whatToExpect.duration: 5 minutes including prep. One quick intramuscular injection.
whatToExpect.frequency: Weekly or monthly, depending on your baseline levels and energy goals.
whatToExpect.howItFeels: A quick intramuscular injection — a brief pinch in the deltoid or glute. Done in minutes.

ingredients.whatItDoes: A B vitamin that is an essential cofactor for enzymes involved in fatty acid synthesis, amino acid metabolism, and gluconeogenesis — all of which directly affect the health of hair, skin, and nails.

personas.headline: Your hair is thinning or your nails keep breaking
personas.detail: Biotin is the primary B vitamin involved in keratin production — the protein that makes up hair and nails. High-dose injection delivers it where oral supplements often can't.

personas.headline: You want to support skin, hair, and nails alongside your IV wellness routine
personas.detail: Biotin stacks well with glutathione — together they address both keratin production and the oxidative stress that contributes to skin aging.

whatToExpect.frequency: Weekly for 4-8 weeks to build levels, then monthly for maintenance.
whatToExpect.howItFeels: A quick IM injection. No significant sensation beyond a brief pinch.

ingredients.name: Glutathione
ingredients.whatItDoes: Your body's master antioxidant — neutralizes free radicals, supports liver detox pathways, recycles other antioxidants, and plays a central role in cellular immunity.
ingredients.whyItMatters: Glutathione is destroyed in the digestive tract, making oral supplements largely ineffective. IM injection achieves dramatically higher bioavailability. It's involved in skin brightening, liver health, athletic recovery, and immune function.

personas.headline: You want skin brightening and antioxidant support in one shot
personas.detail: Glutathione is widely used for skin clarity and an even complexion — it inhibits melanin production while simultaneously improving cellular health.

personas.headline: You've been doing IV wellness and want to add liver and detox support

whatToExpect.frequency: 2-3x per week for cosmetic goals. Weekly for general wellness.
whatToExpect.howItFeels: A brief, quick injection. Occasionally patients notice a mild sulfur-like taste or smell briefly after — this is normal and passes in seconds.

personas.detail: Vitamin D is synthesized from sunlight. Northern latitude + indoor work = almost certain deficiency. This shot restores your levels quickly and completely.

ingredients.whatItDoes: Three compounds that work together to enhance fat metabolism, prevent fat accumulation in the liver, and support bile production for dietary fat digestion.
ingredients.whyItMatters: Methionine is an essential amino acid that metabolizes fat and prevents fat buildup in the liver. Inositol supports insulin signaling and fat emulsification. Choline is essential for fat transport out of the liver.

ingredients.whatItDoes: Boosts metabolic rate at the cellular level and provides the energy support needed when in a caloric deficit.
ingredients.whyItMatters: B12 deficiency can slow metabolism and impair the energy production pathways that support fat burning. Combining it with MIC creates a synergistic metabolic support effect.

personas.headline: You're using a GLP-1 medication and want additional metabolic support

personas.headline: You're working on weight loss and want every tool in the toolkit

whatToExpect.frequency: 1-3x per week during active weight loss. Weekly for maintenance.
whatToExpect.howItFeels: A quick IM injection. No significant sensation beyond a brief pinch.

labTests.name: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
labTests.measuresWhat: Red blood cells, white blood cells, hemoglobin, hematocrit, and platelets.
labTests.whyItMatters: Screens for anemia, infection, immune disorders, and bleeding problems — all at once.
labTests.flaggedBy: Low hemoglobin often explains unexplained fatigue. Elevated WBC can signal active infection. Low platelets flag clotting risk.

labTests.name: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP)
labTests.measuresWhat: Kidney function (BUN, creatinine), liver function (ALT, AST), electrolytes (sodium, potassium, calcium), blood sugar (glucose), and blood protein levels.
labTests.whyItMatters: A full picture of how your organs are functioning — kidney, liver, and metabolic health in one panel.
labTests.flaggedBy: Elevated creatinine signals kidney stress. High liver enzymes can indicate inflammation or fatty liver. Blood sugar flags pre-diabetes or diabetes.

labTests.name: Lipid Panel
labTests.measuresWhat: Total cholesterol, LDL (bad) cholesterol, HDL (good) cholesterol, and triglycerides.
labTests.whyItMatters: The core cardiovascular risk screen. Abnormal lipids significantly increase heart disease and stroke risk — often with no symptoms until it's serious.
labTests.flaggedBy: High LDL with low HDL is the classic risk pattern. High triglycerides often signal metabolic issues (diet, insulin resistance). Low HDL alone is also a risk factor.

personas.headline: You haven't had blood work done recently and want to know where you stand
personas.detail: This panel covers the three most important foundational screens — blood cells, organ function, and cardiovascular risk. Most people have these run annually.

personas.headline: Your doctor recommends routine monitoring
personas.detail: CBC + CMP + Lipid Panel is the standard annual health screen. Fast results, same-day draw.

whatToExpect.onset: Results typically available within 24-48 hours.
whatToExpect.frequency: Annually for most healthy adults. More frequently if managing a chronic condition.
whatToExpect.howItFeels: A standard venipuncture (same as any blood draw). Your nurse explains each test and what to watch for.

labTests.name: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
labTests.measuresWhat: Red blood cells, white blood cells, hemoglobin, hematocrit, and platelets.
labTests.whyItMatters: Screens for anemia, infection, immune disorders, and clotting issues.
labTests.flaggedBy: Low hemoglobin = possible anemia. High WBC = possible infection or immune activation. Low platelets = clotting risk.

labTests.name: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP)
labTests.measuresWhat: Kidney function, liver enzymes, electrolytes, blood sugar, and protein levels.
labTests.whyItMatters: Organ function snapshot — kidney, liver, and metabolic health.
labTests.flaggedBy: Elevated liver enzymes, abnormal kidney markers, blood sugar out of range.

labTests.name: Lipid Panel
labTests.measuresWhat: Total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, and triglycerides.
labTests.whyItMatters: Core cardiovascular risk assessment.
labTests.flaggedBy: LDL/HDL ratio, triglyceride elevation, total cholesterol thresholds.

labTests.name: TSH (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone)
labTests.measuresWhat: The pituitary hormone that drives thyroid function — when elevated, the thyroid is underperforming; when low, it may be overactive.
labTests.whyItMatters: Thyroid dysfunction is extremely common, especially in women, and causes fatigue, weight changes, hair loss, mood issues, and temperature sensitivity — all often misattributed to other causes.
labTests.flaggedBy: Elevated TSH suggests hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid). Low TSH suggests hyperthyroidism. Borderline values warrant further testing.

labTests.name: HbA1c (Hemoglobin A1c)
labTests.measuresWhat: Your average blood sugar over the past 3 months — a much more reliable diabetes screen than a single fasting glucose.
labTests.whyItMatters: Pre-diabetes and early type 2 diabetes are often missed on spot glucose tests. HbA1c catches the pattern. Early detection allows intervention before serious complications develop.
labTests.flaggedBy: 5.7-6.4% = pre-diabetes. 6.5%+ = diabetes. Values below 5.7% are normal.

personas.headline: You want to cover thyroid and blood sugar in addition to the basics
personas.detail: TSH and HbA1c are the two most commonly missed tests on standard annual panels. This package adds them at a meaningful discount.

personas.headline: You have fatigue, weight changes, or mood issues that haven't been explained
personas.detail: Thyroid dysfunction and blood sugar dysregulation are two of the most common and most commonly missed causes of these symptoms. This panel looks for both.

whatToExpect.onset: Results within 24-48 hours.
whatToExpect.frequency: Annually, or every 6 months if managing thyroid or metabolic conditions.
whatToExpect.howItFeels: A single blood draw. Your nurse reviews results with you and can recommend next steps or specialist referral if values are flagged.

labTests.name: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
labTests.measuresWhat: Red and white blood cells, hemoglobin, hematocrit, and platelets.
labTests.whyItMatters: Comprehensive blood cell health and immune status baseline.
labTests.flaggedBy: Anemia patterns, immune activation, clotting disorders.

labTests.name: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP)
labTests.measuresWhat: Kidney and liver function, electrolytes, blood sugar, and protein levels.
labTests.whyItMatters: Organ function across multiple systems.
labTests.flaggedBy: Organ stress, metabolic dysfunction, electrolyte imbalance.

labTests.name: Lipid Panel (Extended)
labTests.measuresWhat: Total cholesterol, LDL, HDL, triglycerides, and LDL particle size.
labTests.whyItMatters: Full cardiovascular risk picture including particle size — a better predictor of risk than standard lipid values alone.
labTests.flaggedBy: Small dense LDL particles, unfavorable ratios, elevated non-HDL cholesterol.

labTests.name: TSH + Free T4 + Free T3
labTests.measuresWhat: The full thyroid panel — TSH (pituitary signal), Free T4 (storage hormone), and Free T3 (active hormone your cells use).
labTests.whyItMatters: TSH alone misses conversion issues between T4 and T3, which are common and cause symptoms even with normal TSH.
labTests.flaggedBy: Abnormal T3/T4 ratio suggests conversion issues. Low Free T3 with normal TSH is a common pattern in symptomatic patients.

labTests.name: HbA1c + Fasting Insulin
labTests.measuresWhat: 3-month blood sugar average plus fasting insulin level — together these reveal insulin resistance before blood sugar becomes abnormal.
labTests.whyItMatters: You can have insulin resistance — the root cause of type 2 diabetes — for years before glucose rises. This panel catches it early.
labTests.flaggedBy: Elevated fasting insulin with normal glucose is the earliest warning sign of metabolic syndrome.

labTests.name: CRP-hs (High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein)
labTests.measuresWhat: A sensitive marker of systemic inflammation, particularly relevant for cardiovascular disease risk.
labTests.whyItMatters: Chronic low-grade inflammation is now recognized as a primary driver of heart disease, metabolic disease, and accelerated aging.
labTests.flaggedBy: Above 1 mg/L increases cardiovascular risk. Above 3 mg/L signals significant systemic inflammation.

labTests.name: Homocysteine
labTests.measuresWhat: An amino acid byproduct of methionine metabolism — elevated levels damage blood vessel walls.
labTests.whyItMatters: High homocysteine is an independent cardiovascular and neurological risk factor, and is directly corrected by B vitamins (B6, B12, folate).
labTests.flaggedBy: Above 15 umol/L is elevated. Usually responsive to B-vitamin optimization.

labTests.name: Vitamin D (25-OH)
labTests.measuresWhat: Your stored Vitamin D level — the best indicator of functional Vitamin D status.
labTests.whyItMatters: Deficiency affects immune function, bone health, mood, and cardiovascular risk. Essential for personalizing your supplementation and IV protocols.
labTests.flaggedBy: Below 30 ng/mL is deficient. Optimal range is 40-80 ng/mL for most adults.

labTests.name: Ferritin + Iron + TIBC
labTests.measuresWhat: Iron storage (ferritin), circulating iron, and iron-binding capacity — together giving a complete iron status picture.
labTests.whyItMatters: Low ferritin causes fatigue, hair loss, and reduced exercise tolerance — even when hemoglobin is still normal. This panel catches iron issues before they progress to anemia.
labTests.flaggedBy: Ferritin below 30 ng/mL is associated with fatigue and hair loss even without anemia.

labTests.name: Comprehensive Hormone Panel (Sex Hormones)
labTests.measuresWhat: Total and Free Testosterone, Estradiol, DHEA-S, Progesterone, FSH, LH.
labTests.whyItMatters: Hormone imbalances cause a wide range of symptoms — low energy, low libido, mood changes, weight gain, sleep disruption — and are often missed on standard panels.
labTests.flaggedBy: Low testosterone in men/women, estrogen dominance patterns, adrenal insufficiency indicators.

labTests.name: Cortisol (AM)
labTests.measuresWhat: Your morning cortisol level — the baseline readout of your adrenal stress response system.
labTests.whyItMatters: Cortisol dysregulation (too high or too low) affects energy, sleep, metabolism, immune function, and stress resilience.
labTests.flaggedBy: Elevated AM cortisol suggests chronic stress activation. Low AM cortisol can indicate adrenal fatigue or insufficiency.

labTests.name: PSA (Men) / CA-125 (Women) — Cancer Markers
labTests.measuresWhat: PSA: prostate-specific antigen for prostate health screening. CA-125: marker associated with ovarian cancer risk.
labTests.whyItMatters: Screening markers that provide baseline values and flag significant changes over time.
labTests.flaggedBy: Elevated PSA warrants urological consultation. Elevated CA-125 warrants gynecological evaluation.

personas.headline: You want a complete picture of your health — not just the basics
personas.detail: This 45+ biomarker panel covers everything from hormones and inflammation to metabolic health, organ function, and cancer screening markers. It's a proper annual deep dive.

personas.headline: You're starting a longevity or optimization protocol and need a real baseline
personas.detail: You can't optimize what you don't measure. The Complete panel gives you the full data set to make informed decisions about your IV protocols, supplements, and lifestyle interventions.

whatToExpect.onset: Most results available within 48-72 hours. Some hormone tests may take longer.
whatToExpect.frequency: Annually as a comprehensive health review. Quarterly if actively managing health conditions.
whatToExpect.howItFeels: A single blood draw — multiple tubes are collected. Your nurse reviews the full panel with you when results come in and can help you understand what the numbers mean.

labTests.name: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
labTests.measuresWhat: Red and white blood cells, hemoglobin, platelets.
labTests.whyItMatters: Baseline blood cell health and anemia screening.
labTests.flaggedBy: Low hemoglobin or iron may explain fatigue.

labTests.name: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP)
labTests.measuresWhat: Kidney function, liver enzymes, blood sugar, electrolytes.
labTests.whyItMatters: Core organ function baseline.
labTests.flaggedBy: Elevated creatinine, glucose, or liver enzymes warrant follow-up.

labTests.name: Vitamin B12
labTests.measuresWhat: Serum B12 levels.
labTests.whyItMatters: B12 deficiency is one of the most common and reversible causes of fatigue, brain fog, and nerve tingling. Vegans, vegetarians, and adults over 50 are at highest risk.
labTests.flaggedBy: Levels below 300 pg/mL may benefit from B12 injections.

labTests.name: Folate
labTests.measuresWhat: Serum folate (vitamin B9).
labTests.whyItMatters: Essential for cell division and DNA synthesis. Low folate contributes to anemia and fatigue.
labTests.flaggedBy: Low folate alongside low B12 suggests a dual deficiency.

labTests.name: Vitamin D (25-OH)
labTests.measuresWhat: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D.
labTests.whyItMatters: Most adults are deficient, especially in Colorado winters. Vitamin D regulates immune function, bone health, and mood.
labTests.flaggedBy: Levels below 30 ng/mL indicate deficiency. Below 20 is severe.

labTests.name: Potassium
labTests.measuresWhat: Serum potassium levels.
labTests.whyItMatters: Critical for heart rhythm, muscle contractions, and nerve signaling.
labTests.flaggedBy: Both high and low potassium are clinically significant.

labTests.name: Iron (Serum)
labTests.measuresWhat: Circulating iron levels.
labTests.whyItMatters: Iron is essential for oxygen transport. Deficiency is the most common nutritional deficiency worldwide and a leading cause of fatigue, especially in women.
labTests.flaggedBy: Low iron with low hemoglobin confirms iron-deficiency anemia.

labTests.name: Magnesium
labTests.measuresWhat: Serum magnesium levels.
labTests.whyItMatters: Magnesium is involved in 300+ enzymatic reactions including energy production, sleep regulation, and muscle function. Most Americans are mildly deficient.
labTests.flaggedBy: Low magnesium is associated with muscle cramps, poor sleep, and migraines.

personas.headline: You feel off but can't pinpoint why
personas.detail: Fatigue, brain fog, and low energy often come down to one or two specific deficiencies. This panel checks the most common ones so you can target exactly what you need.

personas.headline: You want to optimize your IV and injection choices
personas.detail: Instead of guessing which vitamins you need, get data first. Your results tell you exactly where to focus your treatments for maximum benefit.

personas.headline: You suspect a specific deficiency
personas.detail: If you've been tired, losing hair, getting sick often, or having mood changes, one of these markers is likely the answer.

whatToExpect.onset: Results typically available within 2-5 business days.
whatToExpect.frequency: Every 6-12 months for monitoring. More frequently if actively correcting a deficiency.
whatToExpect.howItFeels: A standard venipuncture by a licensed RN. Most patients feel only a brief pinch. Your nurse can review results with you and recommend targeted IV or injection treatments.
